card.title: 3rd CARPATHIAN
card.text: Deployment: Convert a friendly unit into 24th UŁAN.
card.flavorText: The 3rd Battalion of Carpathian Rifles was a unit of the Polish Independent Carpathian Rifle Brigade, formed on 12 April 1940 in French-controlled Syria as part of the Polish Army in France, comprising Polish soldiers who had escaped occupied Poland following the 1939 invasion. Under the command of General Stanisław Kopański, the brigade was modeled after a French mountain infantry unit and initially served under the French Armée du Levant. Following France's capitulation in June 1940, the brigade refused to align with the Vichy regime. On 30 June 1940, it relocated to British-controlled Palestine, integrating into the British Army and reorganizing as a motorized infantry brigade. In August 1941, the brigade was shipped to the besieged port of Tobruk in Libya. There, it played a significant role in the defense against Axis forces, particularly during Operation Crusader, which lifted the siege in December 1941. Alongside their Australian allies, they were nicknamed the "Rats of Tobruk" by German propaganda and reclaimed the name as a badge of pride. On 3 May 1942, it was reorganized into the 3rd Carpathian Rifle Division, forming a core component of the Polish II Corps.
